prompt:

ONE woman standing, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, camera set back so her whole body fits in frame, face still sharp. Mid 20s.

Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. The vessel is already full of water right up to this same straight collarbone line and no higher.

Her real left knee, calf and foot are a separate thing entirely: they simply begin at that same height, flush against the cut face of the glass above them, sharing nothing with it — an ordinary, undisturbed real leg, with real skin, real pores and fine grain, warm in tone, completely opaque, never itself cut, never marked, as if it had always continued naturally from there.

Right leg transition: On the right leg, a little above the knee, the glass vessel ends in a perfectly flat, deliberately cut cross-section, exactly like a clean slice cut through a cast-glass sculpture — at that flat cut face, the full thickness of the glass wall and the clear water sealed inside it are visible edge-on, the cut always clean, deliberate and precise, never jagged or torn, always the finish of a sculpture. Real legs: her real knees, calves, ankles and feet, natural skin texture, standing in a matching pair of extreme platform stiletto sandals.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a soft aqua teal on one side and a pale silver-white on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle — glowing evenly, marked with a few thin dark vertical lines spaced evenly across it so the bending of those lines inside her material body is unmistakable, and a glossy dark floor beneath her feet.

Pose: standing tall, angled 45 degrees, left hand (glass) on her hip, right arm (glass) held clear of her body, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: the glowing backdrop floods her material body from behind, so aqua-teal light passes through one side and silver-white light passes through the other, the vertical lines clearly visible bending inside the glass. A soft frontal light falls on her face, ears and any real leg parts. A thin cool rim light traces her whole figure. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
